A_general.open_code_note: No BambooHR-owned public MCP repository or package was found in the prepared evidence. The documented hosted server is BambooHR-operated; its code and implementation details were not available.
other_official_servers: BambooHR documentation describes the same product server at https://{your-subdomain}.bamboohr.com/api/mcp, a per-customer endpoint using streamable HTTP. It does not document mcp.bamboohr.com/api/mcp as the customer connection URL.
Workato documents a separate BambooHR Self-Service MCP server, a Workato prebuilt server with 9 tools for employee self-service and approver tasks; it is not the BambooHR-hosted MCP endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee or MCP-specific price is stated in the reviewed sources. The hosted MCP server is in beta; customer eligibility and any plan requirements are not specified.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The official pricing page lists Core at $10 USD per employee/month and Pro at $17 USD per employee/month; it also offers a Premium plan with quote-based pricing.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The pricing page describes a monthly per-employee price with volume discounts. It does not state MCP-specific usage charges, call quotas, or rate limits.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The documented connection requires an active BambooHR account, AI Connectors enabled by an administrator, and user inclusion in the selected access audience. The server applies existing BambooHR user permissions. Developer applications are created through the developer portal; dynamic client registration is not supported. The docs state tokens last one hour and refresh automatically for OAuth clients.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization admin; data access is also constrained by the connecting user's BambooHR access level.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official reference lists 56 tools across employees and directory, fields and metadata, datasets, reports, time off, goals, goal comments, hiring, global employment, files, and utilities. The list is for the per-customer URL pattern; the exact global endpoint has no public tool listing.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The docs say the server returns results to the client in MCP format. Detailed result schemas are not published in the tool tables.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The docs describe tools and OAuth endpoints but do not document MCP resources.
No MCP prompt list or prompt capability is documented.
No MCP-specific logging or audit event behavior is documented.

The supplied endpoint responds HTTP 401 with Bearer authentication, realm="apisix", header bearer method, and resource metadata URL https://mcp.bamboohr.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp. That metadata names https://mcp.bamboohr.com as authorization server and publishes scopes_supported. The global origin's unsuffixed protected-resource URL returned 404. The authorization-server well-known responses were not available in the supplied capture; supported grant types, PKCE, token authentication methods, and revocation metadata are therefore not established. Official docs describe OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow, a developer-portal application with redirect URI, no DCR, one-hour access tokens, and automatic refresh for OAuth clients. Tokens carry the permissions of the user who created them.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthorized requests receive HTTP 401. The captured response is an HTML 401 page; successful MCP result/error structure is not detailed in the public reference.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs classify 56 listed tools: most Read, with Write and Delete labels for the modifying operations; the input endpoint's own tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published. 2. The server enforces BambooHR permissions and existing approval/workflow flows; docs recommend clients review writes, but server-enforced confirmation parameters or preview-then-confirm are not documented. 3. OAuth scopes are broad as captured in C; docs say requests run with the caller's BambooHR permissions and administrator-enabled AI Connectors audience. Docs say access can be revoked by disconnecting or disabling the app; token revocation mechanics and redirect-URI review details are not specified. 4. No read-only endpoint, server-side tool filter parameter, sandbox endpoint, or region variants are documented. Claude users can turn off tools in connector configuration; that's client-side. 5. Data access follows BambooHR permissions. Docs describe silent omissions, null/empty restricted values, `_restrictedFields` on list/dataset results, and employee filtering when filter/sort fields are unreadable. File tools list metadata only, not file contents. 6. No MCP call quotas, rate limits, bulk caps, or result truncation are documented. 7. Docs say requests are validated; detailed validation, coercion, unknown-argument behavior, or argument overrides are not published. 8. MCP-specific audit/logging and telemetry behavior are not documented. Privacy notice gives general retention context, not MCP-call logging specifics. 9. No vendor feedback/rating/survey tool is listed. Docs invite feedback through a linked form; no MCP-result upsell mechanism is documented. 10. Docs contain AI-client recommendations, but no server-delivered skills or initialize instructions were found. 11. Memory/state behavior is not documented. 12. The input host is a global-looking endpoint while official connection instructions use customer subdomains; a separate Workato Self-Service MCP is also documented. No nested server routing is described for BambooHR's server. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script, or execute escape-hatch tool appears in the official list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: [Official docs] "Treat an empty or short result as \"nothing this caller can see,\" never as \"nothing exists,\" and never as a permission error."
[Official docs] "Language models are unreliable at date math, so `calculate_date` moves it server-side and returns both a formatted label and structured fields."
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The documented BambooHR-hosted endpoint presents a flat tool list; no hierarchy or dynamic toolsets are documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: An official list exists at https://documentation.bamboohr.com/docs/mcp-server and names 56 tools; its documentation says tools are shown as they appear in an MCP client. Claude's connector directory also reports 56 tools. No catalogue-only tools were added: Pipeworx and Composio describe their own proxy/API integrations, while Workato describes a separate Workato Self-Service MCP server. The official docs describe the customer endpoint as https://{your-subdomain}.bamboohr.com/api/mcp; the input global host has no public tools/list evidence, so the 56 documented names are best-available same-product evidence, not an independently observed list from that host.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim initialize/tool schemas were available. Official docs publish names and short descriptions, but not the serialized MCP definitions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: BambooHR documents that not every product capability is exposed. The MCP list does not include general payroll, benefits administration, employee file-content retrieval, or the full BambooHR API surface. File tools only list metadata and visibility, not file contents. Global employment tools are read-only in the listed MCP set; the public REST API is not a substitute for the MCP tool inventory. Sources: https://documentation.bamboohr.com/docs/mcp-server and https://documentation.bamboohr.com/docs/past-changes-to-the-api.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Claude guide recommends: "Limit the tools you enable." and "Review write actions before approving them." It also says "Verify before you act." These are client/user practices; the docs do not show server-side enforcement of these recommendations. ChatGPT guide says it asks for confirmation before running a data-changing tool, which is client behavior.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The docs state: "The server enforces BambooHR's permissions exactly." They also say "An AI assistant cannot see or change anything you couldn't see or change yourself." AI principles say BambooHR does not use customer-provided data to train or fine-tune third-party AI models for its independent use, subject to stated exceptions. The privacy notice describes general retention and deletion practices.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: BambooHR says users authenticate on its own login page, approve requested access, and can revoke access by disconnecting or by an admin disabling AI Connectors. It warns that responses may be inaccurate or incomplete and recommends checking results.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission enforcement and partial-result behaviors are documented as server behavior. OAuth consent, one-hour tokens, and approval workflows are described, but the endpoint implementation is closed. Client recommendations about confirmation, limiting enabled tools, verifying outputs, and keeping sessions focused are not server-enforced according to the available evidence.

contradictions: The input endpoint is https://mcp.bamboohr.com/api/mcp and returns HTTP 401 with OAuth resource metadata, while official connection instructions specify https://{your-subdomain}.bamboohr.com/api/mcp and warn clients not to use api.bamboohr.com. The host difference is unresolved by the public docs.

The input endpoint's OAuth metadata advertises many scopes covering product areas that are not represented among the 56 tools in the official MCP tool list. The metadata may describe broader OAuth/API scope support; no per-tool scope mapping is published.

The official MCP reference lists 56 tools; Claude connector directory also says 56. It represents the product connector, but does not establish that the global input host exposes precisely the same list.
observations_for_research: The published tool list combines broad HR data reads with a smaller set of write and delete operations, while the OAuth metadata advertises extensive product-wide scopes.
Permission filtering can produce apparently complete but reduced results: some inaccessible fields or employees are omitted without a permission error.
The vendor documents an admin-controlled connection audience alongside user-level permission inheritance; those gates operate at different levels.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, all prepared page text/HTML/script evidence, pricing and legal pages, and repository inventory; no BambooHR-owned MCP source repository or package was present. Official tool list has 56 rows; actions.json was generated from those official table rows. The supplied OAuth capture includes the endpoint POST, the unsuffixed protected-resource 404, and the path-suffixed metadata 200; authorization-server well-known endpoints were not successfully captured. Unofficial BambooHR MCP repositories were listed in links.json and excluded as evidence. The output follows the user-supplied global addressing value, although the official connection docs specify per-customer subdomains.
